descriptions.heading: What each metric means

main.title: ❤️ BPM — Heart Rate
main.text: The number of heartbeats per minute measured from the optical pulse in your fingertip. Normal resting range: 55–90 BPM. Elevated BPM may signal stress, physical exertion, or stimulant intake.

main.title: 🌬️ /min — Breathing Rate
main.text: Respiratory rate derived from the slow amplitude modulation of the PPG signal. Normal range: 12–20 breaths/min. Higher values indicate stress or physical activity; lower values appear during deep relaxation.

main.title: ⚡ Stress %
main.text: Derived from the Cardiac Stability Index. High heart rate variability irregularity → higher stress score. A score under 30 % indicates a calm state; 60 %+ suggests acute physiological stress.

main.title: 🔋 Energy %
main.text: Reflects cardiovascular reserve: how far your heart rate is from its elevated ceiling and how stable the rhythm is. Higher score = more physiological capacity left. Drops with fatigue, high BPM, or prolonged stress.

advanced.title: HRV surrogate (RMSSD)
advanced.text: Root Mean Square of Successive Differences between adjacent RR intervals, in milliseconds. Reflects parasympathetic nervous system activity. Higher = more adaptive autonomic regulation. Typical camera-derived range: 15–70 ms.

advanced.title: Cardiac Stability Index (CSI)
advanced.text: Standard deviation of RR intervals divided by mean RR interval. Measures rhythmic consistency independent of heart rate. Lower values (0.03–0.10) indicate a very stable rhythm; values above 0.25 suggest irregular beats or measurement noise.

advanced.title: Recovery Rate %
advanced.text: How completely the heart rate has returned toward its mean after the highest recorded beat in this session. 0 % = HR still at its peak; 100 % = fully recovered to baseline or below.

advanced.title: HR Trend Slope
advanced.text: Linear regression slope of RR intervals over the measurement window. Negative = heart rate gradually slowing (relaxation response). Positive = HR accelerating (rising arousal or activity).

advanced.title: HR Acceleration
advanced.text: Second derivative of RR intervals — the rate of change of the trend. Positive = HR is speeding up faster than before. Negative = the rate of change is decelerating, even if HR is still rising.

emotional.title: Alarm / Anxiety
emotional.text: Composite of rising HR and elevated breathing rate. High values indicate a fight-or-flight activation pattern in the autonomic nervous system.

emotional.title: Relaxation / Calmness
emotional.text: Inverse of CSI plus energy reserve. High score = low HR variability irregularity, slow stable breathing, and ample cardiovascular headroom — the signature of restful alertness.

emotional.title: Focus / Concentration
emotional.text: Blend of energy level and inverse stress. Peaks when HR is moderate, rhythm is stable, and stress is low — consistent with sustained attentional effort without overarousal.

emotional.title: Excitement
emotional.text: Rises with HR elevation above resting baseline and higher breathing rate. Distinguishable from alarm by the absence of extreme stress scores — it is positive arousal rather than threat response.

emotional.title: Fatigue
emotional.text: Increases when energy is depleted and stress is chronically elevated. Reflects the physiological cost of prolonged effort: reduced HRV, elevated HR at rest, and slow recovery.

emotional.title: Flow
emotional.text: The optimal performance state: high focus, moderate relaxation, and HR slightly above resting without alarm. Appears when you are fully engaged but not overwhelmed — the zone.

descriptions.footnote1: All metrics are derived from the optical PPG signal via the device camera.
descriptions.footnote2: For medical-grade accuracy use a certified biometric device.
